To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Using high-sensitivity Tss prediction with CAGE, we developed a method that identifies, with a high degree of accuracy and in a strand-specific manner, locations on genomes that are highly improbable to be transcription initiation sites.”
we have developed a method that can accurately identify locations in mammalian genomes that cannot initiate transcription.
we developed a methodology and a tool that allows one to predict locations of mammalian genome where transcription is unlikely to initiate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying large portions of the mammalian genome that are not likely transcription initiation locations.
the identification of large portions on the mammalian genome that are highly unlikely (or impossible) to initiate transcription.

the development and application of methods that utilize the information in high-throughput transcriptomic data in order to better understand and predict the transcriptional regulatory mechanisms in mammalian genomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the majority of the mammalian genome is highly unlikely to initiate mammalian transcription.
, based on our analyses, we estimate that on average more then 40% of human genome is highly unlikely to initiate mammalian transcription.
the vast majority of mammalian genome is unlikely to initiate transcription.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a novel method for the prediction of transcription start sites (tssPred) and we used it to estimate the locations of the mouse and human genomes that are unlikely to initiate transcription (ntlPred).
we have developed a methodology for the identification of genomic regions that are highly unlikely, with a high confidence, to initiate transcription in mammalian organisms.
our algorithm allows one to predict, with high accuracy and sensitivity, locations of mammlian genomes where transcription initiation cannot occur.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a substantial portion of the human genome is highly unlikely to harbor TSSs.
the majority of the mammalian genome is not likely to initiate TSSs, and that the majority of genes in mammalian genomes have a single TSS.
a substantial part of mammalian genomes are not prone for transcription initiation.
